title: Three-dimensional Printing of Thermoplastic Materials to Create Automated Syringe Pumps with Feedback Control for Microfluidic Applications
protocol: Download the .STL design files for the syringe pump components from the Supplemental Files.
Prepare the .STL model files for printing by converting them to executable instruction sets for the 3D-printer being used.
Print the plastic components using acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) with a high-quality setting.
Detach the printed parts from the printing platform of the 3D-printer.
Remove the supporting structure from the finished parts.
Fasten the stepper motor to a threaded rod using a motor shaft Z-axis flexible coupler with set screws.
Before continuing, make sure that rotating the stepper motor shaft drives the threaded rod without slippage.
Connect the syringe platform to the motor connector by firmly pressing the syringe platform's connection pegs into the mating holes on top of the motor connector.
Attach the assembled part from step 1.2.1 with the part from step 1.2.2 by fastening four 16 mm screws through the motor connector.
Insert two linear ball bearings and a 0.8 mm hex nut into the openings on the bottom of the traveler push.
Align the threaded rod on the motor connector through the 0.8 mm hex nut in the traveler push.
Insert the two linear shafts through the traveler push and the motor connector.
Place two hex nuts in the hexagonal spaces of the motor connector piece, then use two 16 mm screws to tighten the connections.
Insert a ball bearing into the middle opening of the end stop.
Connect the end stop with the assembled components from step 1.2.7.
Place two hex nuts in the hexagonal spaces of the end stop piece, then use two 16 mm screws to tighten the connections and affix the end stop to the assembly.
Attach the syringe plunger female connector piece to the traveler push piece using two steel lock nuts and two 16 mm screws.
Place a 10 mL syringe on top of the pump.
Ensure the head of the plunger is aligned into the notch of the syringe plunger female connector piece, and the top of the syringe barrel is fixed into the slot of the motor connector.
Insert the syringe plunger male connector piece into the syringe plunger female connector.
Ensure there is a tight fit between the male and female components to secure the plunger in place.
Connect the syringe clamp to the syringe platform using two hex nuts and two 35 mm screws, ensuring the syringe barrel is fixed into the slot of the syringe clamp.
Create the required drawings for a photomask using preferred CAD software.
Print the photomask onto a glass or quartz plate.
Expose the fabricated master mold to fluorosilane vapor in a vacuum desiccator.
Add three drops of fluorosilane to a beaker and place it in a vacuum chamber.
Apply a vacuum for 1 min.
Close the vacuum chamber but keep the master mold inside for 30 min.
Weigh 30 g of PDMS pre-polymer in a weigh boat.
Measure and add a curing agent in a 1:10 ratio to the pre-polymer.
Mix the pre-polymer and curing agent vigorously by hand using a disposable spatula.
Check that there are small, regularly separated air bubbles in the solution after 30 seconds.
Place the master mold in a culture plate.
Carefully pour the PDMS mixture on top of the master mold.
Degas the mixture in a vacuum desiccator for 1 hour.
Ensure no bubbles are observable within the mixture.
Release the vacuum pressure quickly and reapply if any bubbles are present.
Allow the mixture to sit for at least 10 minutes after degassing.
Move the PDMS mixture to an oven set at 90 °C.
Allow the mixture to cure for 30 minutes.
Remove the PDMS from the master mold.
Cut the PDMS into the desired dimensions using a razor blade.
Wear gloves to limit PDMS exposure to contaminants.
File the needle with a metal file or sandpaper to sharpen the blunt ends.
Punch holes for inlet and outlet ports with a 23 G dispensing needle.
Ensure that the punctuated cylinder of PDMS is removed from the needle after every puncture.
Wash the PDMS with filtered deionized water.
Air-dry the PDMS using an air or nitrogen source fitted with a 0.2 μm filter.
Clean a No. 1 borosilicate cover glass substrate with a surfactant.
Air-dry the cleaned cover glass using a pressurized air source fitted with a 0.2 μm filter.
Lightly touch the PDMS with pressure-sensitive tape to remove residual dust without pressing too hard.
Place the PDMS device and a cleaned cover glass into an oxygen plasma cleaner for 1 min.
Ensure the color from the plasma cleaner chamber is bright magenta during the process.
Take the PDMS and the cover glass from the plasma cleaner.
Place the cover glass, face-down, onto the PDMS device.
Gently press the cover glass to the PDMS in a section devoid of molded features if bonding does not occur immediately.
Put the PDMS device in an oven at 90 °C for at least 12 h.
Remove an appropriate amount of wire insulation and shielding from a pressure sensor's electrical cable using a razor.
Connect the wires to male rectangular connectors.
Remove 1 - 2 cm of wire insulation from a stepper motor's leads.
Connect the stepper motor wires to male rectangular connectors.
Affix the syringe onto the inlet side of the pressure sensor.
Connect a 22 G dispensing needle onto the outlet side of the pressure sensor.
Slide one end of 0.51 cm diameter tubing over the 22 G dispensing needle attached to the pressure sensor.
Slide the other end of 0.51 cm diameter tubing over a 22 G dispensing needle connected to the microfluidic device.
Connect the needle to the inlet port of the microfluidic device.
Connect the outlet port of the microfluidic device to a waste disposal reservoir using a 22 G needle and 0.51 cm diameter tubing.
Assemble the electronic circuit on a prototyping breadboard according to the diagram.
Connect the wires from the stepper motor with the stepper motor driver.
Connect the red wire from the pressure sensor to V+.
Connect the black wire from the pressure sensor to V-.
Connect the green wire from the pressure sensor to Signal+.
Connect the white wire from the pressure sensor to Signal-.
Connect the output signal from the breadboard with the analog input pin on the microcontroller.
Connect the logic input pins from the stepper motor driver with the digital pins on the microcontroller.
Connect the STEP input on the stepper motor driver with a pulse width modulated (PWM) port of digital pins on the microcontroller.
Connect the power supply with the breadboard according to the diagram.
Set the power supply to 10 V for the breadboard and the stepper motor driver.
Download and install the appropriate integrated development environment (IDE) for the microcontroller.
Download the controller code titled 'Pressure_Sensing.ino' from the Supplemental Files.
Apply known pressures to the inlet of the sensor with the outlet capped.
Measure the resulting output signal.
Connect a microcontroller to an open-source single-board computer via a serial interface.
Attach a camera module made for the single-board computer to one of the eye-pieces of a stereomicroscope.
Download Timer.h and AccelStepper.h libraries to the microcontroller's IDE library directory.
Download the controller code titled 'Dual_Pump_PID_Control.ino' from the Supplemental Files.
Program the controller code to fit the experiment being conducted.
Modify control parameters or timing parameters to fit the desired response and duration of the experiment.
Compile and upload the code to the microcontroller before running the experiment.
Set setPoint1/2 values in the controller code to change the pressure level.
Adjust stepper1/2Out values in the controller code to adjust the pump speed.
Identify the port number on the microcontroller for the stepper motors from the AccelStepper stepper1/2 column.
Determine the milliTiming variable frequency for reading the analog signal from the pressure sensors.
Set the printTiming variable frequency for outputting speed and pressure values to a serial monitor.
Use a value of 5 for the maxError variable based on the microcontroller's logic level (5 V).
Turn on the power supply for the syringe pumps system.
Set the voltage to 10 V for the stepper motor power supply.
Tune the controller using a manual approach.
Adjust the proportional constant (Kp) to improve the response time of a step function.
Alter the integral (Ki) and differential (Kd) parameters to minimize overshoot and ensure set-point stability.
Set the PID values for Kp, Ki, and Kd variables in the controller code.
